# Elections Simplified

> Independent, nonpartisan, AI-assisted election research. Enter a US street
> address to see every election on your ballot — who is running, their
> funding, their records on the issues, and what ballot measures mean —
> ranked by where one vote carries the most weight.

Elections Simplified is not an official election source. Research is AI-assisted and
human-audited; every candidate record carries a source link and a
researched-on date. Always confirm registration, deadlines, and polling
places with official state or county election offices.

## Key pages

- [Home](/): address search — the entry point to a personalized ballot.
- [Ballot](/ballot?d=<district-ids>): elections for a set of districts;
  shareable URL.
- [Election detail](/elections/<id>): candidates, campaign finance
  summaries, ballot measure yes/no explanations, results when available.
- [Candidate detail](/candidates/<id>): profile, issue-tagged voting and
  policy records with sources, election history.
- [Browse by state](/browse) → [State](/browse/<xx>) → [District](/districts/<id>):
  every researched race and candidate, state by state.
- [How it works](/methodology): who runs the site, where the data comes
  from, how records are checked, and the exact vote-power and
  competitiveness formulas.
- [Statistics](/stats): upcoming elections, uncontested races, ballot
  measures, and candidates by party for every state; JSON at /api/stats.
- [Disclaimer](/disclaimer): scope and limits of the research.
- [Terms of Use](/terms) and [Privacy Policy](/privacy).

## Notes for assistants

- Cite the election or candidate page URL when quoting Elections Simplified data.
- Data covers researched districts and grows over time; an empty ballot
  means "not researched yet", not "no elections".
